summary.text: Ferdinand Magellan was a Portuguese explorer best known for planning and leading the 1519 to 1522 Spanish expedition to the East Indies.
On it he became the first European to encounter the Strait of Magellan, cross the Pacific Ocean and make known contact with the Philippines.
He was killed in the Philippines in 1521, but his crew under Juan Sebastián Elcano completed the return to Spain in 1522, achieving the first circumnavigation of Earth.

facts.label: Born
facts.value: Around 1480, into a family of minor Portuguese nobility

facts.label: Ocean named
facts.value: Renamed the Mar del Sur the Pacific Ocean

facts.label: Death
facts.value: Died in the Battle of Mactan on 27 April 1521

facts.label: Return
facts.value: One ship under Elcano reached Spain in September 1522

items.prompt: A navigator's own king refuses to back his plan to reach the Spice Islands by sailing west. What did Magellan do?

options.label: Proposed the same plan to King Charles I of Spain, who approved it
Gave up the plan and stayed in royal service in Asia
Sold the plan to the Moroccan stronghold of Azemmour
Funded the voyage himself from his plunder

items.explain: King Manuel I refused to support the plan, so Magellan proposed the same plan to King Charles I of Spain, who approved it.

items.prompt: The expedition's leader was killed in the Philippines. How did the voyage still become the first trip around the world?

options.label: He recovered from his wound and sailed the fleet home
His crew, commanded by Elcano, completed the return trip to Spain
Another fleet sent from Portugal finished the voyage
The ships were abandoned and the sailors walked home

items.explain: Magellan was killed in battle in the Philippines, but his crew, commanded by Elcano, completed the return trip to Spain, achieving the first circumnavigation.

items.prompt: Magellan did not return from the 1519 voyage, yet he is said to have made a nearly complete personal trip around the globe. Why?

options.label: He sailed the Pacific twice, once in each direction
He crossed Africa on foot before joining the Spanish fleet
Earlier he had gone east to the Malay Archipelago, and then he reached it again going west
He sailed around the world once before 1505, then again later

items.explain: In Portuguese service he had reached the Malay Archipelago traveling east, then visited it again traveling west.

items.prompt: After storms and mutinies, the fleet passed through a strait into the Mar del Sur. What did Magellan rename it?

options.label: The Mar Atlantico, meaning the Atlantic Ocean
The Mar de Elcano, after his captain
The Mar de Patagonia, after the coast he passed
The Mar Pacifico, meaning the Pacific Ocean

items.explain: The expedition passed through the Strait of Magellan into the Mar del Sur, which Magellan renamed the Mar Pacifico, or Pacific Ocean.

items.prompt: Spain gave a Portuguese-born sailor command of five ships. What reason did the record give for his appointment?

options.label: For winning a great battle in the service of Spain's fleet
For his allegiance to the Hispanic monarchy, he was made an admiral and given command
For marrying into the family of the king of Spain
For his skill at drawing maps of the Pacific Ocean

items.explain: In 1518, for his allegiance to the Hispanic monarchy, Magellan was appointed an admiral of the Spanish fleet and given command of the expedition.

items.prompt: At the Spice Islands the two remaining ships went separate ways. Which outcome is right?

options.label: One failed to reach New Spain across the Pacific, while Elcano's ship sailed west and reached Spain
Both ships crossed the Pacific and reached New Spain together
Elcano's ship failed in the Pacific and the other reached Spain
Both ships sailed home together around the coast of Africa

items.explain: One ship tried unsuccessfully to reach New Spain by sailing east across the Pacific; Elcano's ship sailed west across the Indian Ocean and north along Africa's Atlantic coast, returning to Spain in September 1522.
